text:
jamie: heads up — we're missing pages for a subset of severity=P0 alerts since ~23:01 UTC. customer-facing errors reported for inference-hosting in us-west-2. noticed some gaps in the incident channel automation too. can oncall please take?

priya: on it. seeing the incident-bot didn't escalate to pagerbridge for a bunch of events. looks like 'suppress_on_heartbeat' toggled to true in the webhook envelope? odd. pulling logs.

incident-bot: detected 14 incoming alerts in last 6m. escalation suppressed (policy: heartbeat-window). message: "webhook: suppression active (0x1f)".

matt: @priya any chance config pushed yesterday rolled global suppress flag? i deployed an autoscaling change around 22:50 but didn't touch paging rules.

priya: nope, i only touched autoscale. checking gitops — paging-config.yaml shows no recent change. but pagerbridge logs show repeated 429 from our confirm endpoint. looks like exponential backoff + suppression logic kicked in. snippet from logs: ```
2024-11-13T22:58:43Z pagerbridge api: confirm 429 backoff=120s
2024-11-13T22:59:12Z pagerbridge suppressor: suppression_window=true reason=heartbeat_missing_count>3
```

sara: customers hitting request timeouts? any telemetry?

jamie: yes — some users see 504s and queued tokens failing. severity P0. I'm pinging support to open urgent banner and status page.

priya: can we restart pagerbridge to clear stuck confirm state? i can do a graceful restart in a minute. ops-sre, any concerns?

matt: do a restart. but let's also capture state first. run: ```
sudo journalctl -u pagerbridge -n 200 > /tmp/pagerbridge_journal.log
sudo systemctl restart pagerbridge
```

priya: ran the dump and restarting now. ```sudo systemctl restart pagerbridge```

pagerbridge: shutting down worker-3... ack pending cleared. worker stopped. starting worker-1... started. fresh heartbeat check succeeded.

incident-bot: new events received during restart: 5. escalation policy processed. pages delivered to on-call in us-west now.

sara: confirming: support says banner up, customers seeing reduced errors for new requests. historic errors remain for some inflight jobs.

jamie: good. we should roll a short corrective config: reduce suppression_window sensitivity and add a fail-open fallback that will force pages if confirm endpoint returns repeated 4xx/5xx.

matt: agree. proposed patch: ```
- suppress_after: 3
+ suppress_after: 6
+ fail_open_on_confirm_errors: true
```

priya: will open a hotfix PR and cut canary to staging then prod. tagging @matt for quick review.

matt: reviewing now. LGTM with one nit (log level for confirm failures should stay warn not error).

priya: merged and pushing canary (us-west only). command: ```git push origin hotfix/pagerbridge-failopen && deploy --env=prod-us-west --canary=10%```

incident-bot: canary deployment started. monitoring routes: paging-confirm, webhook-delivery, inc-channel-health.

sara: monitoring shows confirm endpoint success rate jumped to 99.8% in canary. paging resumed.

jamie: action items: 1) postmortem to include sequence (confirm 429 -> suppression -> missed pages) 2) telemetry: add metric for 'escalation_suppressed_due_to_confirm_errors' 3) run tabletop with oncall rotation to validate manual handoff steps. assigning priya to 1 & 2, matt to 3.

priya: ack. starting postmortem draft and adding metrics ticket.

matt: i'll run the tabletop tomorrow at 09:00 PT. invite sent.

jamie: thanks all. we'll keep the status page updated and follow up with impacted customers. filing incident ticket INC-2024-634 in tracker. :thumbsup:

sara: one more note — need runbook update: when pagerbridge confirm returns persistent 4xx/5xx, oncall should immediately escalate to manual paging (theres a toggle) rather than rely on automatic suppressor. adding that to runbook now.

priya: done and pushed. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pagerbridge#fail-open

jamie: closing the thread here but keep adding notes to the incident ticket. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
